prerequisites: Analysis and processing methods for modelling and sizing electrical circuits
Control commands for electrical machines and converters

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the technological issues involved in the design of power modules, through the choice of materials, their positioning within a module and the problems associated with assembly processes.
Propose a cascaded architecture of static converters, with their controls, to meet a specification.
Describe compromises, make choices and apply them through practical implementation.
To know the materials and processes commonly used in the design of a power module
List and implement certain processes for making an assembly
Understand the effect of non-perfect switches and electrical circuits
Understand why a switching aid circuit improves the energy dissipated
Understand the benefits of multi-level architectures
Use simulation tools to validate a conversion architecture for an application

syllabus_topics: Materials, technologies and processes for power electronics integration
Specific work on speed variation: controlled inverters and choppers
Reminder of structures and operation, multilevel inverter structures, mli principle, definition of a mathematical approach for PWM
teaching_methods: Project-based learning (using PRIMES platform, clean room facilities, simulation software like Matlab, Scilab, PSIM, and electrotech lab)
assessment_rules: The evaluation formula is (1*CC1 + 1*SOUT) / 2. This implies an equal weighting of continuous control and the oral exam.
